newsitem.title: USA: Economist sees slow employment growth for Maine.
newsitem.headline: Economist sees slow employment growth for Maine.

text.p: Maine's economy likely will continue to grow slowly at least for the next year or so, predicted Charles Colgan, an economist with the Muskie Institute at the University of Southern Maine.
In the long-term, Colgan said he expected southern and mid-coast areas to experience the most economic gains.
His forecast was delivered Tuesday in Orono at the annual Governor's Economic Development Conference at the University of Maine.

But he projected statewide employment growth for 1996 to be no higher than one-and-a-half-percent. As a result, the economist said Maine will continue to lag behind the nation and the rest of New England.
